title: Why Shared Leads Cost More Than the Price Per Lead
content:
###  **The Advertised Price Is the Smallest Part** 

A shared lead has a sticker price. It also has a set of costs that never appear on the invoice. 

###  **Cost One — The Race** 

A lead sold to four companies rewards whoever calls first. That means someone on your team must be positioned to respond within minutes, all day. Either you staff for that or you routinely lose leads you already paid for. 

###  **Cost Two — The Conversation You Enter** 

By the time you reach the homeowner, they have often spoken to two competitors. The discussion begins at price, because that is the only variable left when three companies are offering the same service in the same week. 

###  **Cost Three — Margin Compression** 

Competing head to head on identical leads pushes quotes down. The lead price is fixed. The margin on the work is what absorbs the pressure. 

###  **Cost Four — No Ownership** 

When the campaign stops, everything stops. Nothing accumulates. There is no residual familiarity in the neighborhood, no repeat effect, nothing that makes next year cheaper than this one. 

###  **The Comparison Worth Running** 

Against that, the relevant question for any alternative channel is not what a lead costs, but what a booked appointment costs — with no competitor already in the conversation.
